source.title: Robust Neural Networks Learning via a Minimization of Stochastic Output Sensitivity
source.authors: Jincheng Li; Wing W. Y. Ng

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares trained neural networks with different explicit regularization methods and reports held-out classification errors, including results for dropout. It does not test the claim's random-label, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, or sharpness versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports comparisons involving dropout, weight decay, noise injection, and SML. Rows below capture the text's explicit dropout comparisons; detailed table values are not reconstructed where the supplied text does not expose them.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates its proposed SML regularizer against other regularizers, including dropout. It never compares otherwise equivalent networks with and without dropout, so its results cannot establish whether adding dropout lowers test error as V6 states. No other claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that SML improves classification relative to several tested regularizers, including dropout, and offers particularly strong robustness when test features contain substantial noise.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains MLP classifiers with an output-sensitivity regularizer and compares them with dropout and other methods; it does not reproduce the claim versions' specified experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported comparison varies dataset and feature perturbation conditions; dropout results are described only in aggregate for the grayscale datasets and comparatively for CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout is reported to outperform weight decay in the grayscale summary and on clean CIFAR-10 BoW features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout can outperform weight decay as an alternative regularizer in these MLP classification settings.

fits_no_version.finding: SMLRFC achieves 24.86% clean CIFAR-10 test error and outperforms the compared regularizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-sensitivity regularization can improve classification of CIFAR-10 BoW features relative to the tested regularizers.

fits_no_version.finding: Under CIFAR-10 feature deletion at p = 0.8, dropout has 82.31% error, weight decay 79.53%, and SMLRFC 38.91%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested regularizers differ substantially in robustness to test-time feature deletion.

record.problems: The dropout comparisons in the prose use weight decay or other regularizers as references, not an unregularized baseline. Numerical dropout comparisons are not stated in the supplied prose, and no random-label or training-error results are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed table entries for dropout comparisons are not separately reconstructed because the supplied text does not expose recoverable values for those entries. No additional dropout result with an explicitly stated numerical value appears in the prose.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its contrast with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit the training set.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
The effect of adding dropout versus no dropout; small-training-set and excessive-dropout qualifications; removal of dropout together with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness and its association with generalization gaps. Input-perturbation sensitivity is a different measure.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the proposed V6 limits_scope verdict: an untested dropout counterfactual is an evidence limitation, not a demonstrated boundary of the claim. Numerical table bodies are absent from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural labels are not compared.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.

No comparison against an unregularized network is reported; the paper does not test the very-small-training-set or excessive-dropout qualifications, nor dropout removal together with weight decay under data augmentation.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap measure.

rows.subject: MLPNN trained with random dropout
rows.operation_detail: Train with random dropout and compare test classification error with weight decay.
rows.baseline: Weight decay; numerical value not stated in the prose result.
rows.value: The paper states that random dropout yields better results than weight decay; numerical value not stated in the prose result.
rows.note: The paper summarizes the comparison across the eight databases, without giving dropout-versus-weight-decay numbers in the prose. This comparison does not isolate the effect versus no explicit regularization.
rows.check: The reported advantage over weight decay is a comparison between regularization methods, not an estimate of the effect of adding dropout. It does not establish partial realization of V6. The prose gives an aggregate summary rather than separate results for each dataset.

rows.subject: MLPNN trained with random dropout
rows.operation_detail: Train with random dropout and compare test classification error with weight decay.
rows.baseline: Weight decay; numerical value not stated in the prose result.
rows.value: The paper states that weight decay yields the largest testing error among the four compared NN training methods; the dropout error is not stated in the prose.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals are reported in Table 6; values not recoverable from supplied text.
rows.note: The prose comparison implies dropout has lower test error than weight decay, but supplies no dropout value. It does not compare dropout to an unregularized model.
rows.check: Lower test error than weight decay cannot establish the effect of adding dropout. The prose also supplies more information than the record acknowledges: Section V-B1 reports SMLRFC error of 24.86% and a 13.02% relative improvement over dropout, implying approximately 28.58% dropout error; this remains an indirect reconstruction.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Eight grayscale image databases and CIFAR-10 comparisons against weight decay
reader_labels.reason: Dropout is reported to outperform weight decay in the grayscale summary and weight decay has the largest error among four NN methods on CIFAR-10, but the study does not isolate dropout against an unregularized baseline (R1, R2).
